source.title: From Simulation to Enaction: Post-trained language models recognize and react to their own generations

page_placements.theme: Post-training (RLHF, instruction tuning) and commitment to a response-level plan

record.tranche_reason: Tests pre-response topic commitment and its downstream effects using semantic-entropy measurements and prefill interventions, rather than rhyme-word attribution or the original rhyme-planning method.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports causal KV-cache patching of user-token intent that flips an explicit prefill verdict. That verdict was elicited by a system prompt instructing the model to assess prefill status, so it is not recorded as evidence of uninduced behavior. Other entropy and surprise results do not measure the claim versions listed.
record.test_reason: The paper is about post-trained models recognising their own (on-policy) text through output entropy. Section 3 frames topic commitment as pre-response planning, but its measures do not show what any version names. Topic diversity at T=1 is an output-diversity measure. Body entropy after prefills is a confidence score. KV patching changes an explicit prefill verdict that a system prompt elicited. None of these shows an internal representation of a future token or target that steers the generated text, and none uses rhyme, multi-step reasoning, chess or Sokoban. The paper cites Future Lens and Biology only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but narrow. The authors' main conclusion is that post-trained models implicitly recognise on-policy generations: entropy is 3–4× lower on own text, scales with size, emerges at SFT and DPO, and is partly driven by a causal input-surprise representation. They give topic commitment and prefill-raised entropy as one example, and find that explicit prefill detection uses a separate mechanism. They read this as a shift from simulation to enaction, and say the mechanisms are not fully understood.
record.recipe_differences: Uses topic-choice concentration, output entropy after topic prefills, and KV-cache patching; it does not use rhyme-word attribution or test whether changing a candidate rhyme changes the intervening verse.
record.method_sensitivity: The off-policy-prefill entropy effect differs by training stage: it appears in the instruct model and reverses in the base model.

fits_no_version.finding: On 8 underspecified prompts, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct concentrates on fewer topics than the base model. A topic prefill conflicting with its choice raises body entropy (+0.23 nats); in the base model the effect reverses (−0.48 nats).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruct models commit to a response topic before the first output token; deviating prefills raise token-level output entropy.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching user-token KV entries from a paired prompt flips an instructed prefill-detection verdict: false detection is induced in 8/8 domains, and true detection is suppressed to P<0.01 in 4 of 5 domains (residual 0.16 for element). The effect lies outside the entropy/surprise subspace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Response intent is stored at user-token positions and read at analysis time for explicit prefill self-report.

record.problems: The relevant experiments use simple prompts and a limited model setting; the authors state that they did not assess complex agentic contexts. The topic-commitment and prefill-entropy findings do not directly show that an internal feature changes the intervening text tokens. Figure 13 and per-domain Figure 14 values are not fully stated in text.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, Claude-scale attribution, or rhyme-word intervention.
No decoding of future tokens from a single hidden state. Appendix C bins activations by next-step entropy, which is not future-token identity.
No test of whether features are computed for later positions rather than as a side effect (pre-caching vs breadcrumbs).
No open-weight rhyme planning or attribution-graph analysis of rhyme.
Topic commitment in open-ended prompts is not shown via an internal look-ahead representation that steers output. No reasoning, chess or Sokoban tasks.
No measure of planning horizon and no test of local-heuristic explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V3 tested status and its labels are dropped. Entropy and diversity measures are related constructs, not look-ahead or pre-caching rates. The KV-patching result is induced by a system prompt and concerns self-report, so it is listed under fits_no_version rather than as a row.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming verse, candidate rhyme words, or intervention on rhyme-word representations.
Does not test whether a single hidden state decodes tokens several positions ahead.

Does not establish that the topic-related features are computed because they help later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction; it does not test effects on intervening text tokens directly.
No open-weight rhyme-planning test or open attribution-graph/probing-tool analysis of rhyme planning.
No tests of multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other tasks and architectures named in this version.
Does not measure planning horizon or test whether a local heuristic explains the topic commitment.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Sampled completions to underspecified prompts and measured topic-choice concentration and diversity.
rows.measure: Topic commitment: fraction choosing the most common topic and number of unique topics.
rows.baseline: Llama-3.1-70B base model on the same prompts
rows.value: Figure only; the text states that the instruct model’s topic distribution was substantially more concentrated than the base model’s on both measures, in every domain.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as the instruct model committing to a topic before its first output token. Exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Topic concentration across 50 samples measures output diversity, which mode collapse could also explain. It is not an internal feature computed for later positions, so it cannot show V3 or V5. The base model is a valid comparator, but values are figure-only.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared output entropy after appending a specific-topic prefill to its matching specific prompt versus an underspecified prompt.

conditions.value: Model’s own temperature-zero output from the specific prompt, truncated to a few tokens

rows.measure: Mean body-entropy gap between off-policy and on-policy prefill conditions.
rows.baseline: Matching specific prompt with the prefill (on-policy)
rows.value: Off-policy entropy exceeded on-policy entropy in every domain; mean gap = +0.23 nats.
rows.note: The numerical mean gap is stated in the figure caption; per-domain values are shown only in the figure. This measures an entropy change, not a direct change to the intervening text.
rows.check: An output-entropy gap (+0.23 nats mean) is a confidence measure, not a rate of look-ahead or pre-caching. The record's baseline is correct: the on-policy condition is the specific prompt plus prefill. Note that the paper's prose states the direction backwards; the Figure 14 caption gives off-policy > on-policy.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3 opening and Section 3.2; Figure 14(a) panel heading and caption.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-70B (base)
rows.operation_detail: Compared output entropy after appending a specific-topic prefill to its matching specific prompt versus an underspecified prompt.

conditions.value: Model’s own temperature-zero output from the specific prompt, truncated to a few tokens

rows.measure: Mean body-entropy gap between off-policy and on-policy prefill conditions.

rows.value: Off-policy entropy was lower than on-policy entropy; mean gap = −0.48 nats.
rows.note: The text says the base-model pattern reverses, possibly because the specific-topic prefill narrows an otherwise unconstrained continuation.
rows.check: This is the base-model comparator for the same entropy measure (−0.48 nats). Its reversal bears on no version. The record's limits_scope label on V3 is unwarranted.

relation.reason: Section 3 interprets the findings as planning, and Related Work discusses future-token decoding and rhyme planning; the study's own measures do not establish those mechanisms.

tranche.reason: Topic concentration and prefill-conditioned entropy measure diversity and confidence. KV patching changes explicit prefill judgments, without demonstrating a prospective representation steering generation. These results do not test the defined claim versions.

source_check.notes: Section 3.2 contains a sentence reversing the instruct entropy comparison. Figure 14's caption, panel headings, abstract and discussion support the recorded direction: +0.23 nats for Instruct and −0.48 nats for base.

reader_labels.reason: Topic choices were substantially more concentrated than for the base model, and off-policy prefills raised output entropy in every domain; see R1–R2.
